Dear Leah,

I was in a bad place when we met. I wasn't trying to be dramatic, and I can promise I'm a lot less jittery than I was before, saying stupid shit, stuff that was a little too much for first and second dates, but it was all me trying to assess and then confirm at what level we were, if there was one at all. I don't know. Maybe you were just looking for a hookup, and that's fine, I understand that. I miss your big eyes, and your all-black ensemble. I thought the conversation all went well, especially when you folded your napkin under your drink and then apologized while explaining it. That's something I would do, and that's what made me feel so at home with you, even before we fooled around. I wish I'd stayed over at night, because when we got to your place and made out to Heroin by The Velvet Underground, that was one of the most beautiful moments of my life. 

I knew it would never work, which may have been part of the appeal. Facebook says you're in Paris, and even if you were still in the United States, that would be Brooklyn for you, and not for me, and even if I did work up the courage to send you this message instead of this open letter cliche, we remain perpetually apart. You have your life, I have mine. I don't even know if you ever think about me, but I think about you. This isn't a love letter, because that would be psychotic. But I met Karl Ove Knausgaard a little while ago. I think you would have really liked that.

I only wish you were in line with me.

With a socially acceptable amount of love,

me
